items.claim: The end boundary before verse 5 splits Jeremiah's complaint from Yahweh's own reply to it at a join without a tier-1 device.
items.evidence: Verse 5 opens on כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ וְאֵ֥יךְ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte) with no introducing formula -- no vayehi-devar-YHWH, no koh-amar, no vayomer, not even a bare attribution clause -- just a reversal of speaker and addressee inside continuous poetry; the row's own rejected-alternative note concedes this directly ('even though no koh-amar or other formula marks that turn'). The complaint and the reply it draws are further bound together by a shared root at their outer edges: כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד, 'all who deal very treacherously' (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte), opens the complaint, and בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ, 'they have dealt treacherously with you' (oshb:Jer.12.6, byte), closes the reply -- the same root framing both halves as one address, left undisclosed here as a device straddling this row's own seam. No parashah mark sits at the verse-4/5 join, while setumah marks flank the outside of the whole exchange instead (closing at oshb:Jer.11.23 just before the complaint opens, and again at oshb:Jer.12.6 where the reply ends; both single-witness, tier-3) -- the marked paragraphing does not divide the complaint from the reply that answers it. Read as a petition addressed to Yahweh answered by a reply addressed back to the petitioner, 1-6 is the shape of one exchange; cutting it at a silent pronoun reversal is a theme-split lacking a tier-1 marker at the cut.
tier_citations: parashah SAMEKH (single-witness, tier-3 in the Prophets):oshb:Jer.11.23
parashah SAMEKH (single-witness, tier-3 in the Prophets):oshb:Jer.12.6

items.claim: The opening boundary at verse 5 is the same unmarked join challenged from the complaint's side, and this row's own device_notes already concede that no formula introduces the reply.
items.evidence: The reply opens on כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ וְאֵ֥יךְ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte), continuing the same second-person exchange rather than opening a fresh discourse event, and the device_notes here already state plainly that no formula marks the turn from complaint to reply at verse 5. The complaint that precedes it (כָּל בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד, 'all who deal very treacherously,' oshb:Jer.12.1, byte) and this reply's own close (בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ, 'they have dealt treacherously with you,' oshb:Jer.12.6, byte) share the same root, bracketing the complaint and the reply as one exchange rather than two; the setumah closing this two-verse span (oshb:Jer.12.6, single-witness, tier-3) is a parashah mark falling where the whole exchange ends, not where this row begins -- there is none nearer, and none at all at the verse-4/5 join it shares with the complaint. Read together with the complaint it answers, 1-6 forms one petition-and-response unit; carrying that reading through is the row's own identified rejected alternative, and the rejection rests on the same unmarked addressee reversal already reflected in this row's own medium_low confidence and raised frontier flag.
tier_citations: parashah SAMEKH (single-witness, tier-3 in the Prophets):oshb:Jer.12.6

items.claim: Verses 7-13 correctly stand as one unit bounded by a genuine tier-1 seam at verse 14, and judgment_oracle is the better fit for material this exchange does not read as address to Yahweh or reply from him.
items.evidence: No koh-amar, word-event, or discourse-frame imperative interrupts 7-13 (byte-checked): the לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ, 'go, assemble,' imperative at verse 9 addresses the field's predators inside the poem's own imagery rather than commissioning the prophet to a new audience, so it does not open a fresh discourse event. The heritage vocabulary that continues past the boundary into the koh-amar oracle beginning כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte) at verse 14 is disclosed in the row's own boundary_rationale rather than concealed. The opening voice-shift at verse 7 (עָזַ֨בְתִּי֙ אֶת בֵּיתִ֔י, 'I have forsaken my house,' oshb:Jer.12.7, byte) reads as a self-standing first-person lament answering no petition and addressing no one in second person, different in kind from the petition-and-reply exchange in 12:1-6 that precedes it -- a distinction a setumah closing that exchange (oshb:Jer.12.6, single-witness, tier-3) corroborates without driving.
tier_citations: parashah SAMEKH (single-witness, tier-3 in the Prophets):oshb:Jer.12.6

items.claim: The koh-amar onset at verse 14 is a genuine tier-1 seam, and folding the restoration clause into one judgment_oracle rather than splitting a salvation_oracle out of it is well-grounded since verse 15 is grammatically subordinate to verse 14.
items.evidence: Verse 14 opens on כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte), turning the address outward to the neighboring nations, a clean tier-1 break from the first-person heritage lament in 12:7-13. Verse 15 opens with וְהָיָ֗ה אַֽחֲרֵי֙ נָתְשִׁ֣י, 'and it will be, after...' (oshb:Jer.12.15, byte), a subordinating construction rather than an independent formula, so keeping it inside the same unit as the judgment governing it is correct rather than an under-split, and the operative-category choice is disclosed as required. The closing neum-YHWH at verse 17 functions here as closure corroboration alone, paired with the fresh command that opens immediately afterward at 13:1 -- a sound use given how densely that formula recurs through the book, where it cannot carry boundary weight verse by verse by itself.

items.claim: Keeping the command, the burial-and-recovery performance, and the interpretation together as one symbolic_act_report is correct, since both internal word-events mark phases of the same enacted sign rather than a change of addressee or scene.
items.evidence: The two internal onsets at 13:3 and 13:8 are both the vayehi-devar-YHWH shape (byte-verified), narrating stages of the same private commission to Jeremiah rather than a new public address; no addressee or scene change interrupts 13:1-11. Keeping the command, performance, and interpretation phases together rather than atomizing them into separate rows treats a symbolic act's three phases as one unit, which is right unless a tier-1 seam intervenes -- and no such seam appears here. The unit is properly bounded downstream by verse 12's own discourse-frame imperative ('and you shall speak to them this word,' oshb:Jer.13.12, byte), which commissions a fresh message to a broader audience distinct from the private belt narrative, so the high confidence recorded here is justified by unusually clean bracketing on both sides.

items.claim: The discourse imperative opening verse 12 is a genuine tier-1 seam separating the wine-jars proverb-oracle from the belt narrative, and judgment_oracle is the correct typing since a spoken proverb turned oracle is not among the book's enacted sign-acts.
items.evidence: Verse 12 opens with a fresh commission ('and you shall speak to them this word,' oshb:Jer.13.12, byte) addressed to a broad audience rather than a continuation of the private belt-recovery narrative closing at 13:11. The unit closes on neum-YHWH at verse 14, immediately followed by a further discourse imperative at 13:15 ('hear, and give ear'), satisfying the requirement that a neum-YHWH closure be corroborated by a fresh tier-1 onset following it. Reading this as an extension of the symbolic-act report was available and correctly set aside, since the belt alone is the enacted sign; the wine-jars saying is spoken to an audience, not performed by the prophet.

items.claim: The imperative opening verse 15 and the imperative opening the next unit at verse 18 correctly bound this row, and rejecting a lament_confession label for the embedded weeping in verse 17 in favor of judgment_oracle is the better reading.
items.evidence: Verse 15's 'hear, and give ear' (oshb:Jer.13.15, byte) opens a fresh address to an audience different from the wine-jars commission just closed at 13:14, and verse 18's 'say to the king and to the queen mother' (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte) opens a new addressee pair, cleanly bounding this row on both sides. The first-person weeping in verse 17 answers no petition and stands inside a warning addressed outward to an audience rather than a plea addressed to Yahweh -- a real distinction from the petition-and-reply shape of the confession material in 12:1-6, correctly kept apart here rather than blurred by content alone.

items.claim: The rejected-alternative argument for stopping at verse 19 leans on an addressee claim at verse 20 that the verse's own doubled Ketiv/Qere note does not cleanly support.
items.evidence: The row reads the material that follows at verse 20 as turning to a second-feminine-singular Jerusalem figure distinct from the king and queen mother, and rests its rejection of the one-sustained-poem rival on that distinctness. But verse 20 carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note on exactly the verb pair in question (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte; single-witness): the consonantal Ketiv reads שאי ... וראי in the feminine singular, while the vocalized Qere actually read by the tradition is the masculine plural שְׂא֤וּ ... וּרְא֔וּ. The 'second-feminine-singular' characterization holds for the Ketiv layer alone; on the Qere, the addressee of verse 20 is grammatically plural, not a lone figure clearly distinct from the royal pair just addressed -- weakening, without disclosing, the very distinction the rejection depends on. This does not overturn the verse-18 opening, a clean discourse imperative to a new addressee pair, but the medium_low confidence and raised frontier flag already recorded here were right to be cautious, and the specific ground offered for closing off the stronger rival needs the Ketiv/Qere split disclosed rather than a clean singular reading asserted.
